correctness.rationale: Absolute summability of the forward jumps gives a finite left limit and an absolutely convergent sum of translated steps. Cardinal partition of unity removes the constant; the compactly supported step derivative has an absolutely convergent series of translates in L¹, giving the upper bound by its L¹ norm. Finite sums converge also to the interpolant (bounded response), identifying the derivative of the limit. The unit step has variation one and attains this bound, and linearity gives the two-input statement. Independently reconstructed both kernels' cell moments and step polynomials. For the six taps the first two excursions have absolute heights 1/81 at t=2/3 and (260+43√43)/5832 at t=(5+√43)/18; the center is monotone by its positive derivative. Reflection from the even partition-of-unity kernel supplies the other two excursions. Their total is 1+4/81+4(260+43√43)/5832. For the four taps the first outer piece is t²(t−1)/2 with extreme −2/27, the middle t(−2t²+3t+1)/2 is strictly increasing, and reflection gives the same variation on the other side. This proves 35/27 and the strict radical excess. Neither endpoint boundary conventions nor sampled-only output variation enter the argument.
residual_risks: The general operator bound follows from the L¹ jump expansion, not random stress checks. No minimax comparison of fourth-order schemes or finite-grid end rule is proved.

value.rationale: This is an exact sharp stability invariant for a widely used accuracy-motivated reconstruction. Measuring full variation exposes both near and far ringing lobes, unlike a pointwise overshoot metric. The unit-step equality and strict four-tap comparison quantify the precise stability cost of this particular classical higher-order choice; the result is useful without a universal comparison across kernels.
residual_risks: No inference to every fourth-order interpolant, nonuniform grid, or multidimensional image TV.
